{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Poland|Cuisine of Poland]] | [[Cookbook:Soup|Soup]]

'''Rosół''' is a traditional Polish meat broth. The most popular variety is Rosół z kury, or clear chicken (hen) soup. It is commonly served with fine noodles, often home made, like Jewish lokshen. It is important to differentiate the type of meat used for the preparation of this particular dish. Young chicken meat will result in a different flavour than that obtained from an older cooking hen. Additionally, the type of meat will result in a different fat content. Finally, other meats, or a mix of beef and/or veal may be used.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
* 1 small [[Cookbook:Leek|leek]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]]s, peeled and sliced lengthwise
* ½ [[Cookbook:Celery Root|celery root]]
* 2–3 sprigs green [[Cookbook:Celery|celery]]
* 1–2 parsley roots
* 1 bunch of [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]
* ⅛ sweet [[Cookbook:cabbage|cabbage]]
* [[Cookbook:Garlic|Garlic]], to taste
* [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|Bay leaf]], to taste
* [[Cookbook:Juniper Berry|Juniper]] seeds
* Dried wild [[Cookbook:Mushroom|mushrooms]]
* [[Cookbook:Allspice|Allspice]], to taste

== Procedure ==
#Quarter the chicken and place in a [[Cookbook:Stock pot|stock pot]] with ~1.5 cold water. Do not add salt at this time, as this may harden some meats. Bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] on high heat, then [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 30–45 minutes. At this time, remove (skim) the surface flotsam (a mix of protein and some fat).
#Add peeled garlic clove, carrots, celery root, parsley root similarly prepared, and other vegetables previously washed.
#[[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] onion halves in minimal oil to caramelize the flesh. Add to the soup. Omitting this step will result in a clearer, less-yellow product.
#[[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] on low heat for approx 2 hours or more. Rosół should not boil, as this will result in a cloudy consistency.
#Season to taste with salt, pepper, bay leaf, allspice, juniper seeds, dried wild mushrooms, etc.
#Continue simmering. You may skim fat off the surface, if so desired (traditionally it should be as fat as possible)
#Remove cabbage, parsley, celery root and any "undesired" vegetables. Carrots are usually left in and served with the broth.
#Serve hot with noodles and fresh parsley. Individuals may season with maggi, [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]], freshly ground black pepper and/or [[Cookbook:Red pepper flakes|chilli flakes]].

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Instead of chicken you may use ½ kg (1 lb) of [[Cookbook:Veal|veal]] or [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]].
* In the traditional Polish way, the chicken is not quartered or cut whatsoever.
* To avoid having to remove surface flotsam use the blanching technique: bring large amount of water (unsalted) to a boil. Remember to leave enough space for the chicken. When in vigorous boil put the chicken in. Let it boil for about a minute. Take the chicken out and put under cold, running water until cold. Now you can add chicken to your rosół, and not worry about the flotsam. It will also make rosół clearer, which is one of the indicators of a good rosół dish.
* Adding vegetable stock or a stock cube is a personal choice. Some argue that it is unnecessary, as the vegetable and meat give enough flavour to the broth.
